column1: # Fixtures the production C codegen REFUSES (exit != 0), and why.
# A fixture here must have NO tests/golden/*.bpf.c: refusing it and also
# shipping a golden for it is the exact contradiction E405 found (78/80/82/96
# say "codegen must reject this" in their own comments, yet had goldens).
# The reason column is prose for the reviewer and is NOT compared — only the
# SET of refused fixtures is. Message wording is the business of
# author needs (what, why, which contexts work, where they wrote it).
# Refresh: ruby tools/golden.rb --update   (and review the diff: a fixture
# appearing here means the codegen started refusing something it compiled.)

column2: unported node: `total += i*i` inside a block (LocalVariableOperatorWriteNode). NOT a C-port regression — the Ruby codegen refuses it identically (E017 ported the `total = total + i` form only).

negative fixture (E392): `param :verbosity` declared, never read. A parameter nothing reads is a switch wired to nothing — the operator sets SPNL_PARAM_VERBOSITY, the output is identical, and "the filter matched nothing" is indistinguishable from "the filter does not exist".

negative fixture (E392): `default:` is not an integer literal. It is baked into .rodata at compile time, so it cannot be an expression; substituting 0 would be worse than refusing (0 is the value that means "off" for a filter parameter).

negative fixture (E399): `filter_by` in a unit that also has an XDP handler. The common filter means "skip this event"; on a verdict hook that would have to be spelled `return 0` (= XDP_ABORTED, or "allow" for lsm/fmod_ret), and on a packet hook bpf_get_current_pid_tgid() reads whichever task is on the CPU. Filtering the kprobe and leaving the XDP open would produce the artefact the feature exists to prevent — a probe that looks narrowed and is not.

negative fixture (E399): `filter_by` declared in a unit with no attach handler it can cover. Same rule E392 applies to an unread `param`: setting SPNL_FILTER_PID produces output identical to not setting it, so "the filter matched nothing" is indistinguishable from "the filter does not exist".

negative fixture (E394): kfield_str_eq with no field path — (ptr, "struct", "literal") leaves nothing to read. Refused at the layer that still knows what the author wrote, with the shape spelled out (including the part that is genuinely easy to get wrong: the LAST string is the literal, not a field).

negative fixture (E395): a sock_* accessor called with no pointer. These are flat calls taking the struct sock * explicitly (D3), so a missing argument must be loud rather than resolved against some `sk` in scope.

negative fixture (E396): has_cap() in an XDP handler. The gate is about MEANING, not loadability -- the read loads in all 24 program types the codegen emits (measure/gate_results.tsv), same as the bpf_probe_read_kernel that ungated kfield uses. Measured (m05): with packets arriving from another machine, the XDP program answered TRUE about a CPU burner while the real actor answered FALSE in a kprobe in the same run. Nothing downstream can tell those apart, so the refusal has to be at compile time.

negative fixture (E396): ns_id(:mount) -- the key selects a kernel struct member at compile time, so the accepted set is closed and a typo has to be loud. Returning 0 would read as "this task is in no mount namespace", which is not a thing, and would then compare unequal to every host check.

spinel-ebpf: attached_symbol_eq: "vfs_open" is not in this handler's list (declared: vfs_read vfs_write). A name that is not attached can never match, so this is refused rather than compiled to a constant false
spinel-ebpf: attached_index is only available inside a multi-symbol handler (`on :kprobe, %w[a b c] do ... end`). In a 1-to-1 handler the attach point is the method name, so there is nothing to ask
spinel-ebpf: on :kprobe, %w[...]: the symbol list is empty -- a handler bound to nothing is a program that loads and never fires (ADR-003)
spinel-ebpf: on :kprobe, %w[...]: duplicate symbol: vfs_read
spinel-ebpf: on :kprobe, %w[...]: `via:` must be :expand or :multi (omit it to let the codegen choose from the list size -- see `spinel-ebpf describe`): kprobe_multi

negative fixture (E411): `on :timer` with no `every:`. The interval is folded into bpf_timer_start at compile time, so a timer without one has nothing to arm. E407 measured what silence costs here — the whole block vanished from the emitted C and the probe still exited 0 — so a timer that cannot fire must not compile.

negative fixture (E411): two `on :timer` handlers in one unit. E079's MVP fixes the callback name (spnl_timer_cb_main), so the second would emit a redefinition and clang would name a symbol the author never wrote. Refused at the layer that still knows there are two blocks.

negative fixture (E411, E399's rule): `filter_by` in a unit that also has a timer. A bpf_timer callback is not process context, so SPNL_FILTER_PID would be compared against whichever task the softirq landed on; filtering the kprobe and leaving the timer open is the "looks narrowed and is not" artefact E399 exists to prevent.

negative fixture (E412): tail_call_to from a kprobe. A tail call lands in a program of the caller's own type, and spnl_prog_array only ever holds this unit's `def xdp_tail__<name>` (XDP). Without the gate the failure is a clang error about an undeclared `ctx` -- a kprobe inner has no ctx parameter at all.

negative fixture (E412): a literal slot outside the declared range. The loader populates exactly one slot per `def xdp_tail__<name>`, in declaration order, and bpf_tail_call into an empty slot does not fail -- it silently falls through, so the symptom is "the fallback path ran" with no signal anywhere. Decidable at compile time for a literal; deliberately NOT decidable, and still allowed, for a computed slot.

negative fixture (E413): reuseport_hash / worker_select from an XDP handler. sk_reuseport shares its AttachKind with six other hooks (sk_msg, sk_skb x2, socket_filter, flow_dissector, sk_lookup) and each has a different ctx struct, so the gate is on the hook NAME. Without it this is two clang errors a layer down -- `struct xdp_md` has no member `hash`, and bpf_sk_select_reuseport's first parameter is a `struct sk_reuseport_md *` -- neither of which names the hook the author chose.

negative fixture (E414): a USER_RINGBUF callback nobody drains. A callback is not attached to anything -- it runs only when some other handler calls user_ringbuf_drain -- so the host could push commands forever with nothing on the other end, and clang would not even keep the function (static, no caller). This is where E414 differs from E412's lone tail-call target, which IS a program and which the loader does register.

negative fixture (E414): two `def user_ringbuf__<name>` in one unit. There is one bpf_user_cmds ring per unit and the drain names its callback by symbol, so the second would be emitted and never called. Same call E411 made for a second `on :timer`.

negative fixture (E414): user_ringbuf_drain with no callback declared. The drain lowers to bpf_user_ringbuf_drain(&bpf_user_cmds, <callback>, ...) and there is no symbol to name. The retired Ruby oracle refused this too; E414 keeps the refusal and says what to write.

negative fixture (E416): a TCP-slice builtin outside XDP. The seven builtins rewrite and RESIZE the raw frame through `struct xdp_md` (bpf_xdp_adjust_tail); a TC classifier holds an skb, and the two syncookie ones bottom out in kfuncs taking XDP packet pointers. Without the gate this is a clang error about `struct __sk_buff` or an unresolved kfunc, neither of which names the hook.

negative fixture (E416): two `xdp__tcp_slice__` in one unit. The generated machine has fixed symbol names and one hardcoded port, so the second is the same program under a second name -- and the emitted C would not compile (duplicate definitions), which reports a C identifier instead of the second `def`.

negative fixture (E416): payload_starts with a non-literal. The prefix is unrolled into one compare per byte at compile time; a non-literal has no bytes then. The alternatives were a matcher that is always true, or a bounded loop -- a different and much more expensive thing than what was asked for.

negative fixture (E420): path_eq on fentry/dentry_open. E418 measured this hook end to end -- it fires and bpf_d_path returns a real string, but the `struct path` belongs to overlayfs's INTERNAL mount, so it renders `/f` rather than the caller's `/tmp/ovd/low/f`, and the control file in another directory rendered IDENTICALLY (hit_ctl_d=1). Selection there matches the wrong file with no symptom anywhere. Asymmetric: emit_path in the same hook is fixture 182 and compiles.

negative fixture (E420): path_starts_with on fentry/vfs_getattr. Same overlayfs rendering as 178, on the other SEC family and the other selector. Doubly misleading here because stat(2) never reaches this hook at all (ftrace: vfs_getattr_nosec 79, vfs_getattr 0 -- E418), so the honest answer names lsm/inode_getattr instead.

negative fixture (E420): path_contains on fexit/dentry_open. Pins the fexit half -- a gate keyed only on `fentry/` would let this through, and E418 measured both sides (h25/h26) as the same rendering.
negative fixture (E420): path_eq on fexit/vfs_getattr, so all four hooks E418 measured have a committed refusal rather than a representative one.
negative fixture (E163): fib_lookup from a kprobe. Gate restored in E405; before that it emitted `bpf_fib_lookup(ctx, ...)` into a ctx-less kprobe inner and clang said "undeclared identifier 'ctx'".
negative fixture (E164): skb_store_byte from XDP. Gate restored in E405; before that the verifier caught it ("program of this type cannot use helper bpf_skb_store_bytes").
negative fixture (E165): skb_load_u32 from XDP. Gate restored in E405; same verifier message as 80.

negative fixture (E178): sk_assign_tcp from tc__egress__. Gate restored in E405; before that it compiled AND loaded — nothing anywhere said the steer could not work, which is why a compile/load gate alone is not enough.
